about: The one source for physical and astronomical constants. Derived values are computed by constants.py and constants.js, not stored. Scenario choices (surface pressure, composition, sites) belong in scenarios/, not here.

exoplasim_3_4_2.note: Unit convention for the installed postprocessor's radius argument. Divide the configured planetary radius by this value to recover its actual radius in the spectral wind transform.
exoplasim_3_4_2.sea_surface_source: ExoPlaSim 3.4.2 seamod.f90 namelist defaults charnock and dz0sea (open-sea roughness max(charnock u*^2/g, dz0sea), with the configured planetary gravity) and fluxmod.f90 parameter vonkarman

swan_41_51_wu.source: SWAN 41.51 swancom3.ftn, WINDP1 and WINDP2 Wu branches; archive SHA256 325c229f3dde0b812db4ec9ae6fa1cd4086d2109562c389576590ce8f94b26bb
swan_41_51_wu.note: The weather-forced wave pilot inverts this drag relation to match atmospheric surface stress. These coefficients describe the pinned wave solver's closure.

cm1_r22.source: CM1 r22.0 src/constants.F, default branch lines 114 and 126; source SHA256 2e02843339a72a428a61bcbd32c27bfbb973766fef842d53200bafaf0ebd3771
cm1_r22.note: These solver closure constants apply to CM1 thermodynamics. Other Terluna compositions use their own gas constants.

used_by: illumination/sky/solver.py (the optical scale height 8 km x 9.80665 / 1.62)
moon_surface_gravity_rounded_m_s2.note: A rounded value. atmosphere/lower_air.py and thermal_column.py use GM/R^2 = 1.62422 m/s^2 (0.26% higher). Moving the users above to GM/R^2 changes the sky atlas, the column set and the A1-A3 references, so it is a recorded decision rather than a silent edit.

notes.optical_libration: Amplitudes of the mean optical librations in longitude and latitude; the ephemeris uses them as sinusoids with the anomalistic and draconic months.
notes.geometric_albedo_visible: Earth's visible geometric albedo varies with cloud cover and viewing geometry; 0.367 is a representative value used for earthlight.
notes.lunar_orbit: Mean orbital eccentricity and inclination to the ecliptic from the NASA GSFC Moon Fact Sheet (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html).
notes.love_numbers: Lunar degree-2 tidal Love numbers: k2 = 0.02405 +/- 0.00018 from GRAIL (Konopliv et al. 2013, J. Geophys. Res. Planets, doi:10.1002/jgre.20097); h2 = 0.0371 +/- 0.0033 from LOLA crossovers (Mazarico et al. 2014, Geophys. Res. Lett., doi:10.1002/2013GL059085). A later global LOLA analysis gives h2 = 0.0387 +/- 0.0025 (Thor et al. 2021, J. Geodesy, doi:10.1007/s00190-020-01455-8).
notes.sun_gm: Heliocentric gravitational constant (TDB-compatible) of the JPL planetary ephemerides.
notes.solar_system_gm: Sun and planetary-system GM values from the DE440 kernel comments / NASA NAIF de440_tech-comments.txt, rounded as published in km^3/s^2 and converted to SI. Existing Earth and Moon values remain unchanged.
